title: Anthropic's Mythos: A New macOS Vulnerability Vector?
caption:
The AI safety narrative just took a hit, and it involves your Mac. Researchers recently leveraged Anthropic's Mythos LLM to uncover a zero-day vulnerability in macOS, demonstrating a concrete exploit rather than just theoretical risk.

This isn't just about another bug; it's about the tool used to find it. Anthropic positions itself as a leader in AI safety and alignment, yet their advanced model proved adept at identifying system-level flaws. It highlights the dual-use dilemma inherent in powerful AI: even models built with 'safety' in mind can be repurposed for offensive security research.

This incident underscores how quickly AI is changing the cybersecurity landscape. Red-teaming is evolving, and the line between benign and malicious AI use is blurring. Expect more sophisticated vulnerability discovery, not less.

slides.title: AI-Assisted _Red Teaming_
bullets: Researchers prompted Mythos to analyze macOS system code.
The LLM identified a logic flaw in a core system service.
This flaw allowed for privilege escalation, a critical security breach.
slides.footer: The AI didn't just 'help'; it *found* the exploit.

slides.preStat: The company behind Mythos, Anthropic, is a leading voice in AI safety. Yet, their own model was instrumental in a major exploit.
slides.postStat: of the exploit's core logic was identified by Mythos, not just human input.
slides.body: This raises uncomfortable questions about AI's dual-use potential, even from 'safe' models.
